identity.name: Tocopherol-rich extract (mixed tocopherols; vitamin E)
identity.chemical_class: Tocopherols (lipophilic phenolic antioxidants; vitamin E compounds)

function.mechanism: Donates hydrogen to lipid radicals and interrupts lipid peroxidation chains, helping prevent oxidative rancidity in fat-containing foods.

adi.basis: Group ADI for the sum of E306-E309 from EFSA 2015 re-evaluation (value extracted from EFSA-indexed record snippet; full text was bot-blocked in this environment).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation for E306-E309 concluded no safety concern at reported uses/use levels and established a group ADI.

fda.notes: 21 CFR 182.3890 and 182.8890 list tocopherols as GRAS with GMP conditions. 21 CFR 184.1890 affirms alpha-tocopherols for limited use as nitrosamine-formation inhibitors in pump-cured bacon.

adi.basis: ADI range 0-2 mg/kg bw for INS 306 (mixed tocopherols concentrate).

concerns.summary: A 2026 prospective cohort study (NutriNet-Sante) reported association between alpha-tocopherol preservative exposure and higher type 2 diabetes incidence; observational design does not establish causality.
High-dose supplemental vitamin E (400 IU/day all-rac-alpha-tocopheryl acetate) increased prostate cancer incidence in SELECT.
A Cochrane review reported no lung-cancer prevention benefit from vitamin E supplementation and identified increased hemorrhagic-stroke risk in one major trial.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2015 re-evaluation (E306-E309) reported no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.
FDA CFR listings indicate GRAS status for tocopherols under specified conditions.
No specific IARC monograph classification entry was identified for tocopherol-rich extract/mixed tocopherols.

adi_exceedance.notes: Routine food-additive exposure appears unlikely to exceed regulatory reference points; concern signals mainly come from supplemental high-dose contexts and observational epidemiology.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory frameworks remain generally permissive (EFSA/FDA/JECFA), with no IARC classification and no major-jurisdiction ban for E306. Residual uncertainty comes from divergent historical ADI frameworks and high-dose supplement safety signals that are not equivalent to typical additive exposure.
key_factors: EFSA re-evaluation conclusion of no safety concern at reported uses
FDA GRAS status in 21 CFR sections for tocopherols
JECFA INS 306 ADI of 0-2 mg/kg bw (older evaluation)
Observational and high-dose supplement signals that do not directly demonstrate additive-level harm
